column3: Ionically Conductive Polymeric Biomaterials and Grafts for Nerve Regeneration
column4: Project NarrativeEvery year over half a million Americans suffer from large-gap peripheral nerve injuries that require surgicaltreatments with neural grafts or engineered graft substitutes but these treatments suffer from limited availabilityand efficacy. Our objective is to address these issues by developing novel ionically conductive biodegradablescaffolds for reliable electrical and chemical stimulation to enhance the regeneration of large-gap nerve injuries.By bridging the knowledge gap between how chemical and electrical stimulation influence cell-materialinteractions and poorly studied nerve regeneration pathways this project has the potential to significantlyenhance large-gap nerve regeneration and functional recovery ultimately benefitting patients suffering fromperipheral nerve injuries.

column3: Enhanced Delivery of Cytotoxic Neural Stem Cells for Treatment of Glioblastoma Multiforme Using an Innovative In-situ Thermogelling Hydrogel and Focused Ultrasound
column4: RELEVANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTHThe benefit of effective and less invasive therapies that can replace invasive surgical procedures and enhancetreatment outcomes for glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) patients is significant. Biomaterial formulations providingsteady and prolonged release over several months of highly effective tumor homing killer cells known as neuralstem cells (NSCs) and the use of a non-invasive dosing method known as focused ultrasound (FUS) to deliverNSCs systemically and across the blood brain barrier (BBB) can potentially increase efficacy outcomes to GBMtreatment regimen and transform the GBM treatment landscape. The overarching goal of this proposal is todevelop and evaluate a new treatment modality that combines a biodegradable and highly tunable biomaterialscaffold and non-invasive FUS to enhance delivery of NSCs to tumor cells and to curb the treatment of GBM.

column3: Novel tunable metformin-releasing injectable scaffolds to enhance dental pulp stem cell-based craniofacial bone regeneration
column4: NARRATIVEPublic Health Relevance: The limited intrinsic regenerative potential of large craniofacial bone defects represents aconsiderable challenge in oral and maxillofacial surgery. The long-term goal of this proposal is to develop novel tissueengineering platforms where mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) with functional organic cation transporters belonging tothe solute carrier 22A gene family can be encapsulated within tunable metformin-releasing injectable scaffolds topotentiate regeneration of vascularized critical-sized bone defects. We anticipate this innovative project will lead tobroader metformin-releasing tissue engineering platforms to benefit many patients in need of oral craniofacial as wellas orthopedic bone regenerative procedures.

column3: Rejuvenating aged bone regeneration by innovative nanomaterials-mediated drug delivery
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVE (RELEVANCE)Repair of large bone defects is a crucial medical challenge and tissue engineering (either usingstem/progenitor cells transplantation and/or growth factors e.g. BMPs) is a promisingalternative to autologous bone graft while a number of crucial barriers must be overcome for fulltherapeutic translation. Through a combinatorial approach utilizing small molecule drugs andtunable and biomimetic scaffolds this study will develop novel regenerating therapies fortreatment of bone defects. The long-term goal of this proposal is to develop novel tissueengineering platforms where mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) with functional organic cation transporters belonging tothe solute carrier 22A gene family can be encapsulated within tunable metformin-releasing injectable scaffolds topotentiate regeneration of vascularized critical-sized bone defects. We anticipate this innovative project will lead tobroader metformin-releasing tissue engineering platforms to benefit many patients in need of oral craniofacial as wellas orthopedic bone regenerative procedures.

column3: Rejuvenating aged bone regeneration by innovative nanomaterials-mediated drug delivery
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVE (RELEVANCE)Repair of large bone defects is a crucial medical challenge and tissue engineering (either usingstem/progenitor cells transplantation and/or growth factors e.g. BMPs) is a promisingalternative to autologous bone graft while a number of crucial barriers must be overcome for fulltherapeutic translation. column3: Novel Therapeutic Approaches For Treatment of Intestinal Inflammation
column4: Project NarrativeThe present Multi-PI application will focus on defining specific factors and cells that may be targeted to treatIBD. We propose here an innovative central hypothesis that nanoparticle-mediated manipulation of TNF IL-12/23 and IL-22 limits established intestinal inflammation and promotes wound healing during IBD. We willexplore this hypothesis with state-of-the-art approaches employing siRNA nanoparticles that target keycytokinesin particular TNF and/or IL-12/23which are involved in the pathogenesis of IBD. Usingcomplementary models of acute and chronic intestinal inflammation we will further define which specificintestinal antigen-presenting cells should be targeted by nanoparticles and the beneficial effect of co-deliveringIL-22 in order to promote wound healing. These studies will help to define novel biological functions ofnanoparticle-mediated siRNA delivery during intestinal inflammation and have the potential to contributemeaningful new findings for the treatment of human IBD.

column3: Novel Therapeutic Approaches For Treatment of Intestinal Inflammation
column4: Project NarrativeThe present Multi-PI application will focus on defining specific factors and cells that may be targeted to treatIBD. We propose here an innovative central hypothesis that nanoparticle-mediated manipulation of TNF IL-12/23 and IL-22 limits established intestinal inflammation and promotes wound healing during IBD. We willexplore this hypothesis with state-of-the-art approaches employing siRNA nanoparticles that target keycytokinesin particular TNF and/or IL-12/23which are involved in the pathogenesis of IBD. Usingcomplementary models of acute and chronic intestinal inflammation we will further define which specificintestinal antigen-presenting cells should be targeted by nanoparticles and the beneficial effect of co-deliveringIL-22 in order to promote wound healing. These studies will help to define novel biological functions ofnanoparticle-mediated siRNA delivery during intestinal inflammation and have the potential to contributemeaningful new findings for the treatment of human IBD.

column4: Project NarrativeHere this proposal is relevant to public health because it seeks to develop virus-inspired nanoparticles topenetrate mucus barriers in diseases (mainly cystic fibrosis (CF)) and effectively deliver gene editingcomponents as gene therapy to correct defective mutations in CF. From these insights we will able to developmore effective drug delivery systems able to penetrate through the complex impregnable mucus barrierpresent in CF. The proposed work is relevant to part of the NIH's mission to help furtherunderstanding biological systems and leveraging that knowledge to improve health and reduce illness.

column3: Novel Therapeutic Approaches For Treatment of Intestinal Inflammation
column4: Project NarrativeThe present Multi-PI application will focus on defining specific factors and cells that may be targeted to treatIBD. We propose here an innovative central hypothesis that nanoparticle-mediated manipulation of TNF IL-12/23 and IL-22 limits established intestinal inflammation and promotes wound healing during IBD. We willexplore this hypothesis with state-of-the-art approaches employing siRNA nanoparticles that target keycytokinesin particular TNF and/or IL-12/23which are involved in the pathogenesis of IBD. Usingcomplementary models of acute and chronic intestinal inflammation we will further define which specificintestinal antigen-presenting cells should be targeted by nanoparticles and the beneficial effect of co-deliveringIL-22 in order to promote wound healing. These studies will help to define novel biological functions ofnanoparticle-mediated siRNA delivery during intestinal inflammation and have the potential to contributemeaningful new findings for the treatment of human IBD.

column3: Chitosan Guided Bone Regeneration Membranes for Dual Local Delivery of Simvastatin and Raspberry Ketone
column4: Project NarrativePatients with craniomaxillofacial injuries periodontal disease and or requiring dental implantprocedures often experience bone loss resulting in complications of masticatory functionspeech and altered aesthetics that affect health and the ability to function in society. Guidedbone regeneration membranes are widely used in these applications to augment bonehealing/regeneration by protecting bone grafted sites but current membranes are not ideal andsuffer high complication rates. This novel membrane will then be able toprovide superior protection and augment healing by reducing inflammation and stimulatingbone formation that will significant improve healing in dental/craniomaxillofacial defectsespecially large traumatic defects.

column3: Novel Therapeutic Approaches For Treatment of Intestinal Inflammation
column4: Project NarrativeThe present Multi-PI application will focus on defining specific factors and cells that may be targeted to treatIBD. We propose here an innovative central hypothesis that nanoparticle-mediated manipulation of TNF IL-12/23 and IL-22 limits established intestinal inflammation and promotes wound healing during IBD. We willexplore this hypothesis with state-of-the-art approaches employing siRNA nanoparticles that target keycytokinesin particular TNF and/or IL-12/23which are involved in the pathogenesis of IBD. Usingcomplementary models of acute and chronic intestinal inflammation we will further define which specificintestinal antigen-presenting cells should be targeted by nanoparticles and the beneficial effect of co-deliveringIL-22 in order to promote wound healing. These studies will help to define novel biological functions ofnanoparticle-mediated siRNA delivery during intestinal inflammation and have the potential to contributemeaningful new findings for the treatment of human IBD.

column3: Retinoids in Vision
column4: NARRATIVEThe retinoid (visual) cycle is a fundamental set of reactions necessary to regenerate the visualchromophore 11-cis-retinal and sustain vision. Genetic or environmental factors affectingchromophore production can lead to blindness. We aim to advance our understanding of theretinoid cycle and to develop strategies to stop progression of human retinal diseases usinganimal models related to this metabolic transformation. Pharmacologic interventions to savevision are now within reach due to a significantly improved understanding of these chemicaltransformations.

column3: Overcoming Immunosenescence by Nanoparticle-Mediated Activation
column4: Relevance to Healthcare Many vaccines are ineffective in elderly patients (>65 years) because of immunosenescence a gradual age-associated deterioration of the immune system. We have developed a particle- mediated adjuvant technology capable of delivering critical immunostimulatory cytokines directly to the draining lymph node the epicenter of the adaptive immune response and where antigen presentation to T cells occurs. By accelerating and maximizing the immune responses to previously non-responsive subpopulations this vaccine technology may significantly improve the healthcare of elderly patients.

column3: A Novel Vaccine to Prevent Urinary Tract Infections
column4: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE: Urinary tract infections are the most common bacterial infection in the United States disproportionately affecting women and exerting a negative impact on health care costs that is estimated at $2.4 billion annually. Although E. coli is known to be the primary cause of disease no vaccine is currently available. The project described in this proposal will develop an E. coli vaccine that combines two innovative technologies: isolation of a unique class of bacterial iron receptor proteins and a nanoparticle delivery system designed to produce a protective immune response in the urinary tract.

column3: Overcoming Immunosenescence by Nanoparticle-Mediated Activation
column4: Relevance to Healthcare Many vaccines are ineffective in elderly patients (>65 years) because of immunosenescence a gradual age-associated deterioration of the immune system. We have developed a particle- mediated adjuvant technology capable of delivering critical immunostimulatory cytokines directly to the draining lymph node the epicenter of the adaptive immune response and where antigen presentation to T cells occurs. By accelerating and maximizing the immune responses to previously non-responsive subpopulations this vaccine technology may significantly improve the healthcare of elderly patients.

column3: Magnetic Delivery of Therapeutic Nanoparticles to the Dental Pulp
column4: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE: Inflammation of the dental pulp or pulpitis is a common painful global public health problem that affects quality of life of patients. In most instances pulpitis is a consequence of repeated insults from thermal stimuli and moderate or advanced tooth decay the most common chronic disease in the world. Available strategies for the treatment of pulpitis are aggressive costly painful and outdated. They are focused at excising the affected hard tissues (cavity preparation) and the placement of a filling or in advanced cases the radical amputation of the tooth pulp-the highly vascularized highly innervated inner layer of the tooth. In this application we describe an innovative technique to deliver medicationslocally to reduce tooth sensitivity and treat pulpitis. We exploit naturally occurring tubules withn the tooth in the dentin layer to magnetically control and deliver biocompatible nanoparticles carrying medications to the tooth pulp. This is a simple conservative and cost effective technique that may cause a paradigm shift in how dentists treat pulpal disease and may prove effective for other dental conditions that affect the teeth such as hypersensitivity and abscesses.
